youtube.title: What Went Wrong With Jaguar's Rebrand?
youtube.description:
The Jaguar rebrand is blamed for one of the worst months in the brand's history: in April 2025 Jaguar registered just 49 new cars across Europe, down from 1,961 a year earlier. Most people point to the pink advert and the new logo, but the showrooms were already emptying.

This documentary traces the Jaguar rebrand failure back to the Reimagine plan written in February 2021, through the Copy Nothing film and the Type 00 concept, to ask why Jaguar sales collapsed and what the other choice would have cost.

This documentary follows the Jaguar rebrand from the 2021 Reimagine plan to the end of the old range, the Copy Nothing film, the Type 00 concept in Miami and the collapse in registrations, with the filings, figures and statements on screen, and asks what the other choice would have cost.

sources.claim: In April 2025 Jaguar registered 49 new cars across Europe, down from 1,961 in April 2024, a fall of 97.5 percent
sources.source: ACEA new car registrations, April 2025 (published 27 May 2025), as reported by Auto Express and Fortune, May 2025

sources.claim: Reimagine announced on 15 February 2021: Jaguar to become a pure electric luxury brand from 2025
sources.source: JLR press release 'Reimagine', 15 February 2021

sources.claim: The electric XJ, close to launch, was cancelled under Reimagine
sources.source: JLR press release, 15 February 2021; Autocar, 15 February 2021

sources.claim: Founded in 1922 in Blackpool as a sidecar maker; Jaguar name used for a model in 1935; company renamed Jaguar Cars in 1945
sources.source: Jaguar Daimler Heritage Trust company history; Paul Skilleter, 'Jaguar: The Complete Story'

sources.claim: Jaguar won Le Mans in 1951, 1953, 1955, 1956 and 1957
sources.source: Automobile Club de l'Ouest official Le Mans results archive

sources.claim: The leaping cat mascot dates from the 1930s
sources.source: Jaguar Daimler Heritage Trust, history of the leaper mascot

sources.claim: Ford bought Jaguar in 1989 for about $2.5 billion
sources.source: Ford Motor Company announcement, November 1989; New York Times, 3 November 1989

sources.claim: Ford bought Land Rover from BMW in 2000 for about $2.7 billion
sources.source: Ford and BMW announcements, March 2000

sources.claim: Tata Motors bought Jaguar and Land Rover from Ford for about $2.3 billion in 2008
sources.source: Tata Motors and Ford announcements, 26 March 2008; completed 2 June 2008

sources.claim: I-Pace named European Car of the Year 2019 and World Car of the Year 2019
sources.source: European Car of the Year jury result, 4 March 2019; World Car Awards, 17 April 2019

sources.claim: Jaguar sold 180,198 cars worldwide in 2018; Land Rover 412,510
sources.source: JLR calendar-year 2018 retail sales release, January 2019 (group total 592,708)

sources.claim: Jaguar sales fell year after year after 2018
sources.source: JLR annual reports and quarterly retail sales releases, FY2019 to FY2024

sources.claim: A new chief executive, previously chief executive of Renault, joined JLR in September 2020 and stepped down in November 2022
sources.source: JLR announcements, 10 September 2020 and 14 November 2022

sources.claim: His successor had been JLR's chief financial officer
sources.source: JLR announcement, 14 November 2022

sources.claim: Britain announced on 18 November 2020 that new petrol and diesel car sales would end from 2030
sources.source: UK Prime Minister's Office, Ten Point Plan for a Green Industrial Revolution, 18 November 2020

sources.claim: In April 2023 JLR set out £15 billion of investment over five years
sources.source: JLR press release, 19 April 2023

sources.claim: New Jaguars to be built on a new dedicated electric platform (JEA)
sources.source: JLR press release, 19 April 2023

sources.claim: The new four-door electric GT to be revealed in 2025 and go on sale in 2026, priced upwards of £100,000
sources.source: JLR statements, 19 April 2023 and 2 December 2024; Autocar, December 2024

sources.claim: The company said it wanted to reach new, wealthier customers and accepted many existing ones would not follow
sources.source: Jaguar managing director interviews at brand launch, November 2024 (Autocar, BBC News, November 2024)

sources.claim: Castle Bromwich built its last Jaguar, the F-Type, in June 2024; XE and XF ended there too
sources.source: JLR statement, June 2024; Autocar, June 2024

sources.claim: E-Pace and I-Pace production at Magna Steyr, Graz, ended by the end of 2024
sources.source: JLR and Magna statements, 2024; Automotive News Europe, 2024

sources.claim: Seven new Jaguar models on sale in Britain in 2018, six in 2023, none new on sale in Britain by 2025; F-Pace built for export
sources.source: Jaguar UK model range 2018 and 2023; JLR confirmation of UK sales pause, November 2024 (BBC News, Autocar)

sources.claim: Brand film released 19 November 2024 with slogans 'Create exuberant. Live vivid. Delete ordinary. Break moulds. Copy nothing.' and no car shown
sources.source: Jaguar 'Copy Nothing' brand film, 19 November 2024

sources.claim: Founder Sir William Lyons: a Jaguar should be a copy of nothing
sources.source: Quoted by Jaguar in its brand launch materials, 19 November 2024

sources.claim: New mixed-case wordmark; the leaper redrawn and kept
sources.source: Jaguar brand identity launch, 19 November 2024

sources.claim: Elon Musk replied 'Do you sell cars?'
sources.source: Elon Musk post on X, 20 November 2024

sources.claim: Jaguar replied: 'Yes. We'd love to show you. Join us for a cuppa in Miami on 2nd December.'
sources.source: Jaguar post on X, 20 November 2024

sources.claim: Type 00 concept shown on 2 December 2024 during Miami Art Week, with no rear window, described as a concept
sources.source: JLR press release, 2 December 2024

sources.claim: JLR reported about £2.5 billion profit before tax in the year to March 2025, led by Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender
sources.source: JLR FY2024/25 results, 15 May 2025

sources.claim: In 2025 JLR's chief executive announced his retirement; Tata named its group finance chief as successor
sources.source: Tata Motors announcement, 31 July 2025

sources.claim: Reports said the design chief behind the new look had left the company
sources.source: Autocar, September 2025

sources.claim: UK ZEV mandate: 22 percent zero-emission new cars in 2024, 80 percent by 2030; £15,000 per car over the line, cut to £12,000 in April 2025
sources.source: UK Vehicle Emissions Trading Schemes Order 2023; Department for Transport announcement, 7 April 2025

sources.claim: Netflix announced Qwikster in September 2011 and lost 800,000 US subscribers in the third quarter
sources.source: Netflix Q3 2011 shareholder letter, 24 October 2011
